options.text: Go by the placards, since they are checked at loading
Correct the shipping papers yourself to match the placards
Deliver the load and report the mismatch on arrival
Not move the shipment until discrepancies are resolved

explanation: Identification must be accurate before transport continues. Use shipper/carrier procedures to resolve it.

distractorExplanations.a: Shipping papers and placards must agree; neither is assumed correct, so the load waits until the discrepancy is resolved.
distractorExplanations.b: The shipper certifies the papers; the driver does not rewrite them but contacts the shipper/carrier to resolve the mismatch.
distractorExplanations.c: Transport should not continue with conflicting hazard information; resolve the discrepancy before moving.

prompt: Emergency response information on/with shipping papers must be

options.text: Available for the materials transported
Kept at the carrier's dispatch office
Provided only for Class 1 and Class 7 loads
Posted on the vehicle beside the placards

explanation: Emergency response information is required to accompany hazmat shipments. ERG pages or equivalent emergency information qualify.

distractorExplanations.b: Emergency response information must travel with the shipment and be immediately accessible to the driver and responders.
distractorExplanations.c: Emergency response information is required for most hazmat shipments that need shipping papers, not just explosives and radioactives.
distractorExplanations.d: Emergency information stays with the shipping papers in the cab; the vehicle exterior carries placards, not response guidance.

prompt: When evacuating an area for a hazmat release, a key principle is?

options.text: Move people downwind where the air is clearer
Move people upwind and keep them away from vapors
Move people downhill, away from the spill site
Gather everyone close to the vehicle to keep a headcount

explanation: Protect by distance, wind direction, and denying entry. Use guidance distances to decide how far.

distractorExplanations.a: Downwind is the direction vapors travel; evacuate people upwind and uphill of the release.
distractorExplanations.c: Heavier-than-air vapors flow downhill; move people upwind and uphill, not downhill.
distractorExplanations.d: Staying near the vehicle keeps people in the hazard zone; move them to a safe distance upwind before counting.

prompt: A driver who discovers a suspected radioactive package with damaged integrity should

options.text: Move the package to the cab to keep it under watch
Wrap it in plastic and reload it away from people
Minimize time near the package, maximize distance/shielding
Continue the trip because the package label shows Radioactive White-I

explanation: Time-distance-shielding and expert response apply to radiological concerns. Isolate the area and notify authorities and the carrier.

distractorExplanations.a: Bringing it closer increases exposure; time, distance and shielding mean staying away and isolating the area.
distractorExplanations.b: Handling a damaged radioactive package adds exposure and spreads contamination; isolate it and wait for qualified help.
distractorExplanations.d: White-I means low surface radiation for an intact package; a damaged package needs isolation and notification.

prompt: Hazmat security awareness training is required so employees can

options.text: Recognize and reduce security risks
Classify materials and select placards
Respond to spills using the ERG
Pass the TSA background check

explanation: Security plans/awareness reduce intentional misuse of hazardous materials. Risks include theft, tampering, or terrorism targeting hazmat.

distractorExplanations.b: Classification and placarding are covered by function-specific training; security awareness targets threats like theft and tampering.
distractorExplanations.c: Emergency response training covers spills; security awareness training is about recognizing and responding to security threats.
distractorExplanations.d: The TSA threat assessment is for the HME driver; security awareness training is required for every hazmat employee.

prompt: A suspicious person photographing a chlorine tank terminal for no legitimate reason should prompt

options.text: Asking them to leave and taking no further action
Reporting to security/law enforcement per site procedures
Confronting them and seizing the camera yourself
Waiting to see whether they come back a second or third time

explanation: Unusual surveillance of hazmat sites is a reportable security concern.

distractorExplanations.a: Unusual surveillance of a hazmat site should be reported; just sending the person away loses information security needs.
distractorExplanations.c: Employees should avoid confrontation; the correct step is to note details and report to security or police.
distractorExplanations.d: Suspicious activity is reported promptly; waiting for repeat visits gives a possible attacker more time.

prompt: Selective transportation security measures for certain high-risk hazmat include

options.text: A placard showing the high-risk status on the vehicle
Sharing route details with any caller who asks for them
Enhanced security plans and route/communication practices
Using any route as long as the shipment is placarded

explanation: Higher-risk materials trigger stronger security plan requirements. Attendance and securement rules also apply as required.

distractorExplanations.a: Placards are hazard communication for every placarded load; they are not an added security measure for high-risk materials.
distractorExplanations.b: Route and schedule information is protected under a security plan and shared on a need-to-know basis.
distractorExplanations.d: High-risk materials may require designated routes and route planning; placarding does not permit any route.

sourceNote: Original UniPrep2Go local bank (Wave 2).

prompt: Enroute security includes:

options.text: Parking at isolated rest areas overnight to stay out of public sight
Leaving the engine running when stepping out briefly
Sharing route plans on the CB to get traffic updates
Minimizing stops, locking vehicles, and being aware of tailing

explanation: Reduce opportunities for theft/hijack of hazmat. Watch for tampering as well.

distractorExplanations.a: Isolated spots invite theft or hijacking; secure, well-lit, attended locations are preferred.
distractorExplanations.b: A running, unlocked truck is an easy theft target; lock the vehicle and take the keys at every stop.
distractorExplanations.c: Broadcasting routes and load details gives would-be attackers information; keep route details need-to-know.

prompt: A broken cargo seal that you did not expect may indicate

options.text: Possible tampering—follow company procedures and report
A routine seal failure from road vibration
A shipper error to fix by resealing and going on
Nothing to report if the placards are still in place

explanation: Seal integrity is a security control; anomalies need response. Document it before proceeding.

distractorExplanations.b: Seals rarely break from vibration; an unexpected broken seal is treated as possible tampering until checked.
distractorExplanations.c: Resealing without reporting hides possible tampering; follow company procedures and report before continuing.
distractorExplanations.d: Placards say nothing about cargo access; a broken seal signals possible tampering that must be reported.

prompt: CDL hazmat endorsement generally requires:

options.text: A knowledge test and a clean driving record for 3 years
TSA security threat assessment plus knowledge testing
A skills test in a placarded vehicle plus a medical card
Carrier hazmat training records instead of a CDL test

explanation: Federal security threat assessment is part of hazmat endorsement issuance. The TSA process includes fingerprint-based background checks.

distractorExplanations.a: A clean record is not the requirement; the HME needs a TSA security threat assessment with fingerprints plus the knowledge test.
distractorExplanations.c: There is no hazmat skills test; the endorsement requires the hazmat knowledge test and the TSA threat assessment.
distractorExplanations.d: Employer training is required separately but does not replace the hazmat knowledge test and TSA assessment.

prompt: Employees should report threats or suspicious purchases of precursors when

options.text: Police have already opened an investigation
Only after a second suspicious visit by the same person at the counter
Behavior suggests planning to misuse hazardous materials
A manager confirms the buyer is not a regular customer

explanation: Early reporting can prevent incidents; follow company/law enforcement channels.

distractorExplanations.a: Reporting should not wait for an official investigation; employees report when behavior suggests planned misuse.
distractorExplanations.b: Waiting for repeat visits delays a report that could prevent an attack; report as soon as behavior seems suspicious.
distractorExplanations.d: Reporting depends on suspicious behavior, not customer status; regular customers can also show signs of planned misuse.

prompt: Access to hazmat storage areas should be

options.text: Open to any employee of the facility during work hours
Unlocked during the day when staff are on site
Granted to drivers who show a valid CDL
Limited to authorized personnel with controls

explanation: Physical access control is a core security measure. Controls include locks, badges, and escorts as required.

distractorExplanations.a: Access is limited to authorized personnel with a need to enter, not every employee on shift.
distractorExplanations.b: Being staffed does not control access; storage areas stay locked or badge-controlled during working hours too.
distractorExplanations.c: A CDL does not authorize entry to storage areas; access depends on authorization and site controls.

prompt: Which communication practice is more secure for high-risk load details?

options.text: Need-to-know sharing over secure company channels
Broadcasting UN numbers and routes on public CB for entertainment
Posting manifests on public forums
Texting strangers the gate code

explanation: Limit sensitive logistics details to authorized parties.

distractorExplanations.b: Public radio spreads targeting info.
distractorExplanations.c: Public posts are insecure.
distractorExplanations.d: Gate codes are sensitive.

prompt: Vehicle attendance requirements for certain explosives/hazmat mean

options.text: The driver must stay inside the cab at all times
Someone qualified may need to attend the vehicle
A locked vehicle counts as attended for Class 1
The driver may watch it from a sleeper berth

explanation: Attendance/surveillance rules reduce theft and unauthorized access—know the material-specific requirements. The specific rule set may require keeping it within view.

distractorExplanations.a: Attendance means being awake, not in the sleeper berth, within 100 feet and with a clear view of the vehicle; staying in the cab is not required.
distractorExplanations.c: Division 1.1–1.3 vehicles must be attended by a qualified person; locking the vehicle does not meet the rule unless it is on a safe haven.
distractorExplanations.d: A person in the sleeper berth is not attending; the attendant must be awake and within 100 feet with the vehicle in view.

prompt: If you suspect your placarded load is being followed by an unknown vehicle engaging in hostile surveillance, you should

options.text: Pull over on the shoulder and let the vehicle pass
Speed up and take back roads to lose the follower
Avoid confrontation, note details, and contact law enforcement
Drive straight on to the receiver and report it once the delivery is done

explanation: Personal safety and reporting beat vigilantism. Carrier security should also be contacted per procedure.

distractorExplanations.a: Stopping on a shoulder makes the truck an easy target; keep moving toward a safe, populated area while reporting.
distractorExplanations.b: Evasive driving with hazmat raises crash risk and can lead into isolated areas; stay on route and contact police.
distractorExplanations.d: Hostile surveillance is reported right away to police or carrier security, not after the delivery is complete.

prompt: Tamper-evident devices help by:

options.text: Physically stopping entry to the cargo area
Replacing the need for padlocks on high-risk hazmat loads
Recording who opened the trailer and when it happened
Showing whether unauthorized access to cargo may have occurred

explanation: Seals complement locks; they detect intrusion attempts.

distractorExplanations.a: Seals are not barriers; they show evidence of access, while locks are what physically resist entry.
distractorExplanations.b: Tamper-evident seals complement locks rather than replace them; they reveal intrusion but do not prevent it.
distractorExplanations.c: A basic seal shows only that access may have occurred; it does not log identities or times like an electronic lock.

prompt: A security plan for hazmat employers typically addresses

options.text: Personnel security, unauthorized access, and en-route security measures
Spill response steps, ERG isolation distances, and first-aid procedures
Placarding, package labeling, and shipping paper accuracy checks
Driver hours of service, logbook audits, and required rest breaks

explanation: Plans systematically reduce risks of theft/misuse.

distractorExplanations.b: Spill response belongs to emergency response planning; a security plan covers personnel, access and en-route security.
distractorExplanations.c: Hazard communication rules cover papers and placards; the security plan addresses theft and misuse risks.
distractorExplanations.d: HOS rules are separate FMCSA requirements; security plans focus on personnel checks, access control and en-route security.

prompt: Carrying unauthorized passengers or allowing unknown persons into the cargo area of a hazmat load is

options.text: Acceptable if the person rides in the cab only
A serious security and safety violation
A minor issue unless the load is Class 1
Permitted if the passenger has a CDL

explanation: Control of the vehicle and cargo is fundamental security.

distractorExplanations.a: Unauthorized passengers are not allowed in a CMV even in the cab; carrier authorization is required under 49 CFR 392.60.
distractorExplanations.c: Unauthorized access is a serious violation for any hazmat load, not just explosives.
distractorExplanations.d: Holding a CDL does not authorize someone to ride along or enter the cargo area; carrier authorization is required.

prompt: Which action best supports both safety and security at delivery?

options.text: Drop the trailer at the gate if the receiver is closed
Hand over the load to anyone signing the bill of lading
Verify receiver authorization and document exceptions
Remove placards before arrival to stay inconspicuous

explanation: Identity verification and documentation prevent diversion. Check seals and IDs per procedure.

distractorExplanations.a: Leaving a loaded hazmat trailer unattended at a closed site invites theft; follow carrier instructions for secure parking.
distractorExplanations.b: A signature alone does not prove authorization; verify the receiver's identity and authorization before handing over.
distractorExplanations.d: Placards must stay on while hazmat is aboard; removing them breaks hazard communication rules and does not improve security.
